method_summary: Easy-example proposal selection (min LPIPS disagreement per class group) paired with uniform time sampling. 256 samples x 4 proposals = 1024 generated, 256 selected. Uniform weighting. This is the exact opposite joint configuration of round-01 (max-LPIPS + early-scale bias).

causal_hypothesis.proposal_selection: Among multiple teacher proposals per class, samples with MINIMUM LPIPS distance from the initialized student provide the cleanest, most stable gradient signals. Hard-example selection (round-01, max-LPIPS) picks outlier or noisy teacher proposals that cause destructive overfitting gradients at the 256-sample budget. Easy examples represent the typical teacher distribution, giving reliable gradients that don't mislead the student.
causal_hypothesis.time_distribution: Uniform time sampling across all 10 FM scales provides balanced gradient coverage. Early-scale power-law bias (round-01) concentrated ~52.5% of mass in scales 0-1, starving mid-to-late refinement scales. One-step generation must produce both global structure and fine details simultaneously, so all scales need adequate gradient signal.
causal_hypothesis.rationale: Round-01's joint strategy (max-LPIPS + early-bias) underperformed baseline by +0.46 FID at 256 samples. Because both factors changed simultaneously, we cannot isolate which caused the harm. Testing the exact opposite joint configuration (min-LPIPS + uniform) is the most informative diagnostic: if it improves over round-01, at least one factor was harmful; if it beats baseline, the opposite joint is genuinely effective; if it similarly underperforms, 256 samples may be insufficient regardless of strategy.
causal_hypothesis.attribution_note: This is a joint two-factor comparison with round-01. The result alone cannot decompose individual factor contributions. A minimum of two more single-factor perturbation runs would be needed for full isolation, which may not be budget-justified.

next_step_decision_rule.if_improved_vs_r01_and_baseline: If FID < round-01 (10.127) AND FID < baseline (9.663): the opposite joint strategy works. Next step: scale to 1024 samples with same min-LPIPS + uniform strategy to see if improvement scales with data.
next_step_decision_rule.if_improved_vs_r01_not_baseline: If FID < round-01 (10.127) but FID >= baseline (9.663): the direction change helps but isn't enough at 256 samples. Next step: increase to 1024+ samples with this strategy, or test a single-factor isolation run.
next_step_decision_rule.if_same_as_r01: If FID ≈ round-01 (within ~0.3): both selection direction and time distribution are similarly ineffective at 256 samples. The problem is likely sample count, not strategy. Next step: jump to 1024+ samples with default/uniform strategy.
next_step_decision_rule.if_worse_than_r01: If FID > round-01 (10.127): round-01 strategy was actually better, meaning hard-example mining has value but early-bias time may have been the culprit. Next step: test max-LPIPS + uniform time to isolate the time factor.

differences_from_round_01.comparison_type: Joint two-factor flip. Does NOT isolate individual factor contributions.
